page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked up to 3.9 GHz. The virtual machine provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical dedicated cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The underlying processor features a massive 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography accelerators like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes a baseline network throughput of 15 Gbps and contains no local storage or bundled GPUs, requiring networked block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance across compute, memory decompression, and specific vector processing tasks. In Geekbench, the instance achieves 2,043.0 in single-core and 17,097.0 in multi-core metrics, scoring within the top 25%. Compression operations are notable, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 223.94 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 33.51 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects 133.67 GB/sec in large uncached read blocks and 63.0 GB/sec in large writes. Cryptographic throughput on the PassMark test scores 36,285.59, and overall PassMark CPU capacity reaches 51,024.22. Small-model LLM generation benchmarks place the server in the top 10% with 404.39 tokens/sec on a 135M model, though larger 70B parameter models display expected CPU-bound bottlenecks, dropping to 2.71 tokens/sec during generation.

Resource allocation provides solid cost efficiency for architectures demanding dense DDR5 memory coupled with modern vector instructions. Because it provides dedicated vCPUs with 256 GB of RAM, workloads avoid memory contention while benefiting from wide instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512 without the overhead of GPU provisioning. The primary operational tradeoff stems from the complete absence of bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O must route over network-attached storage. Consequently, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, big data ETL processing, and enterprise application tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors delivering 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores) at 3.9 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 256.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled GPUs, and no local disk storage, necessitating remote volumes for file systems. Benchmarks show upper-quartile results in Geekbench multi-core, single-threaded gzip compression, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and CPU encryption tests. The memory configuration is balanced toward high-density memory workloads rather than disk-intensive storage profiles, making the r8i.8xlarge well suited for in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, enterprise data processing, and lightweight model inference.
